turns.prompt_text: What is a good multimeter that can measure current?
turns.response_html:
Most multimeters can measure current, but the "best" one depends on whether you need to measure low current (like for electronics) or high current (like for home wiring) and whether you need to measure AC or DC.

For most general purposes, there are two main types of tools to consider:

  1. Digital Multimeter (DMM): Best for electronics and small appliances. You measure current by connecting the meter "in series" (breaking the circuit). These are very accurate for lower currents (milliamps up to 10 Amps).
  2. Clamp Meter: Best for electrical work and high power. You measure current by clamping the jaw around a wire without touching live parts. These are safer and easier for high currents (e.g., 100+ Amps) but often less accurate for small electronics.

Here are three top recommendations covering these different needs:

Top Recommendations

Best Overall & Professional Choice: Fluke 115 RMS Digital Multimeter The Fluke 115 is widely considered the gold standard for general-purpose use. It is a "True-RMS" meter, meaning it provides accurate readings even on non-standard signals. It can measure both AC and DC current up to 10 Amps (20A overload for 30 seconds). It is highly durable, safe (CAT III 600V rated), and ideal if you want a tool that will last for decades and cover almost any task from automotive to electronics.

Best Value for Basic Use: Klein Tools MM325 Digital Multimeter If you need a reliable meter for occasional home or auto tasks without the professional price tag, this Klein model is a strong choice. It is durable (2-meter drop protection) and covers the basics like voltage, resistance, and continuity. Note that for current, it is designed primarily for DC current (up to 10A), which is perfect for automotive and battery projects, but it does not measure AC current (household power) effectively.

Best for High Current & Safety: Klein Tools CL220 Digital Clamp Meter If your main goal is to measure current in household wiring (like checking how much power an appliance uses), a clamp meter is much safer. The CL220 measures AC Current up to 400 Amps simply by clamping around the wire. It also functions as a standard multimeter for voltage and resistance (via test leads), making it a versatile "hybrid" tool for homeowners.

Quick Comparison

Here is a detailed comparison to help you decide which features match your needs:

If you are planning to work on specific electronics (like computer parts) versus household wiring (like outlets), I can suggest a more specific accessory kit (like magnetic hangers or fine-point probes) to go with your meter.

Best Digital Multimeters 2025 review This video provides a hands-on review of the Fluke 115 and compares it against other top models, demonstrating why it is often chosen for its accuracy and reliability.

Based on the model number provided, you are looking for the Ideal 61-327 Digital Multimeter.

This is a Manual Ranging Multimeter designed for basic electrical testing in residential or light commercial settings. It is a rugged, entry-level meter often used for checking outlets, switches, and batteries.

Key Features

  • Voltage Measurement: Measures up to 600V AC and DC.
  • Manual Ranging: You must manually select the correct range (e.g., 20V, 200V, 600V) on the dial for your measurement, unlike "Auto-Ranging" meters that do this for you.
  • Non-Contact Voltage (NCV): Features a sensor at the tip that detects live voltage (40V–600V) without touching the wires—useful for quickly checking if an outlet is "hot."
  • Battery Test: Dedicated settings for testing 1.5V (AA, AAA) and 9V batteries under load, which gives a more accurate reading of battery health than a standard voltage check.
  • Safety Rating: CAT III 600V (Safe for household wiring and switches).

Important Limitation: No Current (Amps)

This meter does NOT measure current (Amps). Unlike many other multimeters, the 61-327 does not have a setting for AC or DC current (A/mA). It is strictly for measuring Voltage, Resistance, Continuity, and Diodes.

  • If you need to measure current (amp draw of an appliance), you would need a different model, such as the Ideal 61-337 or a clamp meter.

Verdict: This is a solid, durable tool for a homeowner or maintenance tech who needs to verify power is off, check for broken circuits (continuity), or test batteries. However, if your work involves troubleshooting motors or measuring power consumption, this meter will not work for you.
